lag.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/3] The stability coefficients across 6 years are moderately high [/page/9/Text/7] cross-tabulating cluster membership between age 43 and 49 using the earlier indicated LICUR procedure. We then looked for significant types, that is, cluster membership combinations across age that occurred more frequently than expected by chance. The results are summarized in Fig. 2. First the six developmental typical patterns that would indicate individual stability were significance tested. All except one was significant, indicating that starting at age 43 you ended up in a similar cluster more often than expected by chance. The exception was Cluster 43:4 (characterized by very low Global Life-Satisfaction), which was not significantly linked to belonging to Cluster 49:4 six years later.
